## Detailed PR specification — COR23AC

**Problem and result.** Account failure-contract tests accept responses missing the contract they claim to enforce. A corrected test lane must fail when success/statusCode/code disappear or validation errors change shape, while preserving successful checks of the currently intended responses.

**Primary files.** treehammock.Tests/Integration/ApiValidationEnvelopeTests.cs and AccountAdjustIntegrationTests.cs. **Implementation.** Require a JSON object with correctly typed success, statusCode and code; assert false, the expected HTTP/envelope status and exact expected error code. Check the expected account validation error array, field names and nonempty string message lists. Preserve route-specific data/result assertions and agree null/omission behavior for optional data/errors rather than silently allowing unrelated schemas. Remove the status-only branch and object-map validation compatibility from these account assertions. **Executable acceptance.** Run both affected HTTP suites in the actual host. Missing/malformed body, invalid identifiers/password/country/factor fields, protected-route denial, adjustment validation/duplicate/stale trust and required-key 428 must retain exact envelopes. In a disposable mutation run, replace model-state envelope registration with the framework default and require the relevant HTTP tests to fail for schema/code differences even when status remains 400. Also make a required-key denial omit or alter its code while retaining 428 and require that test to fail. Restore the production path and prove the same cases pass. Retain discovery and results under COR01/COR24; source text assertions alone cannot close this finding.

**Dependencies.** The schema correction can be implemented against the current behavior without waiting for every domain fix. Final execution requires a working SDK/restore lane and configuration consistent with COR23L; later security/privacy changes must update expected responses deliberately. Coordinate the eventual shared helper with R10F, whose full suites remain unreviewed here. This PR owns R10E-01 only; related domain findings retain their earlier owners.

**Migration/rollback.** Test-only change; no schema migration or public API change. Reverting assertions would restore the verification hole. ## Detailed corrective PR — COR23AD

**Title:** Dispose owned two-factor flow factories after each test.

**Problem/result:** Fifteen tests leave their factory-owned application lifetime without explicit teardown. The PR makes each helper-owned factory stop and dispose when its owning test finishes or exits exceptionally.

**Files:** `treehammock.Tests/Integration/AccountFlowRegressionTests.cs`; add a focused lifecycle test/support probe only if needed to verify host stop/disposal. Shared factory changes are unnecessary unless the selected ownership API needs a reusable fixture helper. No application endpoints, schema, authentication behavior or delivery policy changes are part of this PR.

**Implementation:** Give `LoginTwoFactorHarness` explicit ownership via `IAsyncDisposable` delegating to its factory and change all fifteen test allocations to `await using`. A scoped factory in every caller is an acceptable alternative if equally explicit. Keep client scopes inside the owner lifetime; stop/dispose the host once after requests complete. Make creation/cleanup exception-safe. Existing twelve scoped factory cases must retain correct ownership. Also close JSON document lifetimes in helper call sites that currently discard returned documents; prefer helpers returning only needed values or explicit caller scopes. Keep these cleanup changes in the same PR rather than creating an additional finding.

**Validation:** Execute the complete account-flow suite on the pinned SDK/package graph. Use a disposable DI service/hosted-service probe to observe normal host shutdown and disposal, including an intentional exception after host start that is caught by the lifecycle test. Assert disposal happens exactly once and the original exception remains observable. Cover a harness whose factory never starts. Repeat the focused lifecycle cases in one process to detect undisposed probe instances; no timing or memory threshold alone substitutes for observing ownership cleanup. Confirm all existing flow assertions continue to pass and that no later test accesses a disposed factory.

**Acceptance:** Every owned factory has a test/fixture teardown owner; host/server/provider cleanup is observed after normal and exceptional exits; no shared host is accidentally disposed by an individual request. Publish the discovered tests and outcomes. Static `await using` presence alone does not close the runtime cleanup criterion.

**Dependencies/order:** Can land independently of production corrections; COR01 supplies result evidence and COR24 includes it in integrated qualification. Do not delay cleanup until all authentication PRs are implemented. No migration or deployment sequencing is needed. Rollback changes test lifetime only and reopens this finding if teardown is removed.

## Detailed corrective PR — COR23AF

**Title:** Bind authenticator replacement grant targets consistently through the repository.

**Owns:** R23B-01 only. **Depends on:** COR08, COR16, COR23B and COR23. **Coordinates with:** COR23C actual reader qualification; COR24 runtime qualification.

**Files:** Repos/AuthenticatorAppEnrollmentRepo.cs; Rigging/Security/SensitiveActionTargets.cs; focused actual repository and service regression cases. Inspect Controllers/AccountTwoFactorController.cs and Services/AuthenticatorAppProvisioningService.cs as the current upstream target contract.

**Implementation:** Build the repository's canonical target with the command's expected predecessor enrollment ID and version, matching the controller and service. Preserve grant validation, expected identity/version SQL arguments, fresh setup null predecessor behavior, account/session/purpose binding and fail-closed mismatches. Use the current typed target helper; do not accept a target made for a different predecessor or omit predecessor binding to permit replacement.

**Regression cases:** A fresh setup with null predecessor succeeds. A grant-bound replacement carrying the current predecessor ID/version reaches actual PostgreSQL and commits the new encrypted enrollment. A stale identity/version, changed label/required/provider, missing grant or target made for a different predecessor is denied with retained state. The actual repository negative control that removes the two predecessor arguments must fail the valid replacement case, not merely compile or trip a lexical witness. The service/controller and repository must agree on canonical target shape.

**Acceptance:** Compile and execute the production repository/service path using real PostgreSQL, grant consumption, enrollment-bound v2 material and an independent durable-state observer. Publish exact passing cases and failing mutation evidence, retaining all native prerequisites and original gates. Source comparison alone cannot close this finding. Review result readers under the existing COR23C scope, without moving its ownership here.

**Schema policy:** Direct current pre-1.0 contract edits; no upgrade, compatibility or backfill strategy. No schema change is expected. Record append-only implementation/qualification history and keep old unbound entry points denied.
